title: A/B Test and Online Experiment Under Diminishing Marginal Effects: Regret Minimization and Statistical Inference

problem.claim: Online sequential experiments with diminishing marginal effects must optimize traffic allocation and support valid inference for the expected reward under the optimal allocation.

gap.claim: Classical algorithms can fail to provide valid statistical inference in this setting.

contributions.claim: Develops an online algorithm using a smoothness condition on how marginal effects change.
The algorithm achieves the best achievable expected cumulative reward.
The algorithm satisfies a valid central limit theorem for statistical inference under the optimal traffic allocation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Numerical experiments serve to illustrate the theoretical findings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diminishing marginal effects can occur when online platforms vary the fraction of user traffic receiving a strategy.
This phenomenon complicates sequential experiments because the optimal allocation may mix strategies rather than assign all traffic to one strategy.
The work targets adaptive optimal traffic allocation and valid central-limit-theorem-based inference when the optimal allocation is unknown.
Classical algorithms may fail on the inference task.
A new smoothness-based algorithm is shown to achieve optimal cumulative reward and valid inference, with numerical illustrations.

source_observation.claim: When per-user effects diminish with broader traffic deployment, the reward-maximizing allocation may be a mixture of strategies.

interpretation.claim: Traffic allocation should be modeled as a potentially interior optimization problem rather than assumed to favor a single strategy.

application.claim: Online experimentation systems should jointly optimize allocation and inference under deployment-dependent effects.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the mixture structure or smoothness-based approach applies beyond the stated setting.

unknowns: The exact smoothness condition is unspecified.
The algorithm, regret criterion, and comparison baselines are unspecified.
The numerical experiment design and results are unspecified.
The scope and assumptions of the central limit theorem are unspecified.
